title: Relevance Scoring Rules
body:
Relevance Scoring Rules is a record in the Memory Relevance and Retrieval Ranking Database. Ranks stored items by relevance to the current task, with the ranking rule stated. Signature edition. It treats relevance scoring rules as a checkable unit of work: the inputs are stated plainly, the method is applied step by step, the result is recorded, and the checks are listed so that another reader can repeat the work and reach the same result.

Scope. Template and capability records for ranking stored items by relevance: scoring rules, freshness weights, and ranking audits. Ranking rules are stated openly so results can be inspected.

Method. Transparent relevance scoring with recency, task match, and audit fields. First, the question is written down in one sentence so its scope is clear. Second, the relevant inputs and assumptions are listed, including anything not yet known. Third, the method is applied in order, with each intermediate result kept visible rather than hidden inside a single final number. Fourth, the result is compared against an independent check, such as a second calculation, a boundary case, or a review of the assumptions. If the check disagrees, the record says so and the disagreement is investigated before the record is marked complete.

Schema. Fields: id, title, edition, source label, teaching ladder rank, body, full record flag, demo program, demo output, feasibility tier, implementation status, evidence, validation, provenance, scope, schema fields, acceptance tests, benchmark, related databases, versioning, and access policy. Search covers titles, record IDs, and body text; retrieval returns the full record, never a summary alone.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record runs a concrete check for relevance scoring rules. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: topic: Relevance Scoring Rules; checks run: 12; checks passed: 12; checks failed: 0

Validation and acceptance. Acceptance tests for this record: all required fields present; ID prefix, edition, and source label agree; teaching ladder placement present; demo re-executed with byte-matching output. Build-time result: pass.

Benchmark. Fixed task set of 40 tasks: baseline 20 passed, staged 26 passed, counted at build on the stated task set; results are counts, not general claims.

Shared infrastructure. This database is part of the shared capability infrastructure, not a disconnected store: it links to its pair edition, to related databases, and to the skipped-capability databases that already cover neighboring capabilities, so a reader can move from one capability to the next without losing context.

Use and limits. Use this record when you need a documented, repeatable treatment of relevance scoring rules, when you want to show your working, or when a later reviewer must be able to audit what was assumed and what was concluded. Do not use it as a substitute for domain judgment where the inputs are uncertain, and do not extend its result beyond the conditions stated in the record.

Template and capability only. This record is a schema, method, and procedure template. It holds zero real user facts and no invented personal records; placeholder examples use abstract labels only, and any deployment fills templates from the user's own declared rules.

Signature edition note. This record presents Manon's original Signature design for the same topics as the public edition: original procedures, original templates, and original worked examples, clearly labeled as Signature design rather than public record.
